clue.text: Might it be used against dishonest shop-assistant?

definitions.text: Might it be used against dishonest shop-assistant?

parts.words: Might it be used against dishonest shop-assistant?
parts.note: read the phrase as proof gathered at the shop counter, the till where a crooked assistant might be caught out

explanation.surface: A store detective wonders what would catch a light-fingered sales clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: A shop assistant works behind a counter, so proof against one is, punningly, evidence from the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof that contradicts a claim, here punned as proof taken from behind the shop counter.

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a tail is the rear end of something

explanation.surface: A cigarette butt that has been snipped off early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog-end' reads as British slang for a cigarette butt, but it splits into dog and end.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail something is to shorten or abridge it.

parts.note: a boxer's rising punch is named as a cut from below, so the word for higher, followed by cut, names that blow

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the word for 'higher' joined to 'cut' gives the boxing punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher in position, and with cut added it names a rising blow in boxing.

parts.note: a trench is a long narrow ditch
an ant is the crossword's standard worker, from the worker ants of a colony

explanation.surface: A labourer who digs ditches speaks bluntly.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant remarks are incisive and outspoken, as a forthright person is.

clue.text: Gentleman brought up fish and meat dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word for gentleman is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sir is the title of a knight, a gentleman
sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: A gentleman is served fish and a meat course.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat, a type of meat dish.

clue.text: Virginia went round a headland for the butterfly

indicators.note: the Virginia abbreviation and the 'a' together go round the headland word, one on each side of it

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia rounded a cape to find a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: Virginia looks like a woman's name; it is the state abbreviation VA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanessa is a genus of butterflies including the red admiral and painted lady.

clue.text: Do we have right to life interest in it?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are entitled to a lifetime share of an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue reads as the question a widow might ask about her husband's estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dower was a widow's share for life of her late husband's estate, a life interest in it.

indicators.note: other suggests a different arrangement of the word one

parts.note: something portable is light enough to carry

explanation.surface: A person names a further lamp that can be carried around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges ONE into EON; 'portable' reads as describing the lamp but gives LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A neon light is a glowing gas-discharge tube, a kind of lamp used in signs.

parts.note: someone who stops being outside a room or group has gone in

explanation.definitionFit: To have gone in, or joined, is to be no longer outside.

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, as in redo
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Laundry instructions say to put something under the iron a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to hold down or subdue, keeping someone under control.

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A new book was left behind in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Shropshire is an English county on the Welsh border; NEWPORT is a market town in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Newport is a market town located in that English county.

clue.text: Very bad tragic actor promises to pay

indicators.note: tragic suggests the word actor has met a disaster and been knocked out of shape

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A dreadful performer playing tragedy can only offer promissory notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means appalling or of terrible quality.

indicators.note: first tells us the word for control comes before the other piece

parts.note: to rule is to control
R is the abbreviation for take, from the Latin recipe on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A governor's first act is to seize power.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'take' comes from prescriptions; 'first' puts RULE ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is one who governs a state or people.

parts.note: to lug is to drag or pull something heavy
a gage is a kind of plum, as in greengage

explanation.surface: Someone tugs a plum out of the shopping bags.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is a traveller's baggage, the bags and cases carried.

explanation.surface: Doing well in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both prospering or making progress, and growing old.

indicators.note: awry means askew, so the letters of edge and all are set crooked

explanation.surface: Someone announced that every border was crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleged means asserted or claimed without proof, as when something is declared.

parts.note: an overwhelming election win shares its name with a perilous slip of earth down a hillside

explanation.definitionFit: A crushing election win is named after a collapse of a hillside, which is dangerous.

clue.text: One or two vessels used for washing

definitions.text: One or two vessels used for washing

parts.words: One or two vessels used for washing
parts.note: a single washing vessel whose name is made from two other words for washing vessels

explanation.definitionFit: A tub to bathe in is one vessel whose name joins two words for washing vessels.

clue.text: Companion trapping leading player gets the bird

indicators.note: trapping means the companion word encloses the other piece

parts.note: bud is short for buddy, a companion
a star is a lead performer

explanation.surface: A friend who has captured the lead actor ends up getting booed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' suggests being jeered; here it just introduces the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustard is a large ground-dwelling game bird of open country.

clue.text: Daring villain holds attorney up during display of self-confidence

indicators.note: holds means the villain word contains the other piece

parts.note: a bravo is a bold hired thug or assassin

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the attorney word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A bold rogue lifts a lawyer aloft during a show of swagger.
explanation.walkthrough: A bravo is an old word for a hired cut-throat; 'Daring' leans to the surface but is part of that description.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is boastful show of courage, a swaggering confidence.

indicators.note: a rendition is a performance or version, so the word for Tuscans is rendered in a new order

explanation.surface: People from Tuscany perform a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sanctus is the hymn beginning 'Holy, holy, holy' sung in the Mass.

indicators.note: unending means the word such loses its final letter

parts.note: cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: So much endless taxation on wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Success is the attainment of wealth or a flourishing state.

clue.text: Leaves on the table available for the sultan

parts.note: salad is leafy greens served at a meal
in can mean available, as in stock

explanation.surface: Lettuce served at dinner is ready for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Saladin was the 12th-century sultan of Egypt and Syria who fought the Crusaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the famous Muslim ruler of Egypt and Syria in the Crusades era.

definitions.meaning: a single image from a film, a frame

explanation.surface: A snapshot of a distiller.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is both a single photograph from a film and the apparatus used for distilling spirits.

parts.note: Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: An English composer has departed the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: LARNE is a ferry port in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Larne is a harbour town in County Antrim with ferries to Scotland.

clue.text: Derived from forefathers coming from Lancaster

indicators.note: coming from suggests the answer is produced out of the letters of Lancaster rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone whose lineage traces back to a Lancashire city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' signals a rearrangement of LANCASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral means inherited from or relating to earlier generations of a family.

clue.text: Again go over rhythmic "monologue in city" — just the opposite

indicators.note: the clue says monologue in city, but the opposite holds: the city goes inside the monologue

parts.note: rap is spoken rhythmic verse
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A city's rap performance is being reviewed in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's quoted phrase spells out one container; 'just the opposite' tells the solver to swap which piece holds which.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise, running over the points once more.

clue.text: Unusually large one, first of all, in the country

indicators.note: unusually means the word large appears in an uncommon order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: first of means take only the opening letter of all

explanation.surface: An exceptionally big individual leads the way within a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African nation.

clue.text: Clearly showed one boy holding another

indicators.note: holding means the first boy's name contains the second

parts.note: Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward
Vince is another boy's name

explanation.surface: One lad hugging another made his feelings plain.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to reveal or display a quality plainly.

clue.text: It is not safe to use during hostilities

definitions.text: It is not safe to use during hostilities

parts.words: It is not safe to use during hostilities
parts.note: suggests caution in wartime, but describes an arm that is hazardous to anyone

explanation.definitionFit: A hazardous arm, such as a knife or gun, poses a risk to anyone nearby.
